title: Representing and Evaluating Parse Trees as Python Dictionaries
description: Build nested dictionary trees for 2 + 3 * 4 and 7 - 2 - 1 to see how tree depth and nesting decide precedence and associativity.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: `leaf(val)` returns `{"node": str(val), "children": []}` and `tree(label, *children)` wraps child nodes in a list. `pretty(t, indent=0)` prints `t['node']` indented by `"  " * indent` and recurses on each child with `indent + 1`.

`evaluate(t)` computes the value of a tree bottom-up. If `t["children"]` is empty (line 23), it returns `float(t["node"])`. Otherwise, line 26 evaluates every child first (`vals = [evaluate(c) for c in t["children"]]`) before applying `op` on lines 27-30.

Lines 46-48 build `correct_tree` with `"+"` at the root and `tree("*", leaf(3), leaf(4))` as its second child. Lines 51-53 build `wrong_tree` with `"*"` at the root and `tree("+", leaf(2), leaf(3))` as its first child.
Look at line 26 alongside lines 46-53. `vals = [evaluate(c) for c in t["children"]]` finishes every child before the parent's operator runs. Whichever operator sits deeper in the tree executes first.

steps.question: On lines 66-69, `left_tree` nests `tree("-", leaf(7), leaf(2))` as the left child of `"-"`, while `right_tree` nests `tree("-", leaf(2), leaf(1))` as the right child. What float values do lines 68 and 69 print?

steps.description: Lines 66-69 build and evaluate `left_tree` (`4.0`) and `right_tree` (`6.0`) for `7 - 2 - 1`.
Inside `evaluate(correct_tree)`, the inner child `tree("*", leaf(3), leaf(4))` multiplies `3.0 * 4.0` to return `12.0` on line 28. The outer `"+"` then adds `2.0`.
